root_cause.text: The memfd_luo preserve logic captured the dirty flag of a folio only at preserve time, but a folio could become dirty after that point (e.g., after preserve but before freeze), causing the serialized state to incorrectly mark it as clean, which on retrieval allows the new kernel to reclaim the folio under memory pressure, leading to user data loss.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "memfd preservation with LUO saves the flag at preserve(). This is problematic. The folio might get dirtied later. ... After retrieve, the next kernel will see the folio as clean and might try to reclaim it under memory pressure. This will result in losing user data." The patch applies the fix by unconditionally marking all folios dirty (folio_mark_dirty) and always setting MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY, removing the conditional check.

    mm: memfd_luo: allow preserving memfd
    
    The ability to preserve a memfd allows userspace to use KHO and LUO to
    transfer its memory contents to the next kernel.  This is useful in many
    ways.  For one, it can be used with IOMMUFD as the backing store for IOMMU

This ensures no folio can become dirty after the flag is captured, thus preventing the data loss described. The vulnerable construct (dirty flag captured before freeze) is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `memfd_luo_preserve_folios`, the dirty flag is captured at preserve time via `folio_test_dirty(folio)` (line ~117).
